secoes.titulo: Estrutura da frase, artigos e classes de palavras
Tempos verbais, aspecto e sequência temporal
Verbos modais, condicionais e voz passiva
Inferência fina, falsos cognatos e integração gramatical

questoes.enunciado: In the sentence “The report that the committee submitted was unusually detailed”, the clause “that the committee submitted” modifies the noun “report”.
questoes.explicacao: The clause is a defining relative clause: it identifies which report is being discussed and functions as a postmodifier of the noun “report”. It does not modify the verb “was”.

questoes.enunciado: In “Although the figures were incomplete, the analyst published the summary”, the word “although” introduces a purpose clause.
questoes.explicacao: “Although” introduces a concessive subordinate clause, indicating contrast between incomplete figures and publication. Purpose is commonly expressed by “so that” or “in order that”, not by “although”.

questoes.enunciado: In the noun phrase “a remarkably efficient system”, the word “remarkably” functions as an adverb modifying the adjective “efficient”.
questoes.explicacao: “Remarkably” is an adverb of degree or manner modifying the adjective “efficient”; “efficient” characterizes the noun “system”. The article “a” determines the singular count noun phrase.

questoes.enunciado: The definite article in “The elderly are more likely to need assistance” is used before an adjective to refer to a whole class of people.
questoes.explicacao: The pattern “the + adjective” can denote a group sharing a characteristic. Here, “the elderly” refers collectively to elderly people and takes a plural verb, as shown by “are”.

questoes.enunciado: In “She gave me useful advice”, the noun “advice” is plural because it refers to several recommendations.
questoes.explicacao: “Advice” is an uncountable noun in standard English and does not normally take a plural ending or the indefinite article. Several recommendations can be expressed as “pieces of advice” or “recommendations”.

questoes.enunciado: In the sentence “The newly appointed director addressed the staff”, the word “newly” is an adjective modifying “director”.
questoes.explicacao: “Newly” is an adverb modifying the past participle “appointed” within the participial adjective phrase. The adjective phrase “newly appointed” modifies the noun “director”.

questoes.enunciado: In “What the witnesses described surprised the investigators”, the initial clause functions as the subject of the main verb “surprised”.
questoes.explicacao: The wh-clause “What the witnesses described” is a noun clause functioning as the subject of “surprised”. Its internal object is the thing described, and the main clause is “surprised the investigators”.

questoes.enunciado: In “There are several reasons for the delay”, the word “there” refers to a previously mentioned place and is the sentence’s adverbial of location.
questoes.explicacao: Here, “there” is an existential introductory subject, not a locative adverb. The notional subject is “several reasons”, which explains the plural agreement in “are”.

questoes.enunciado: In “By the time the inspectors arrived, the equipment had been removed”, the past perfect passive indicates that the removal occurred before the inspectors’ arrival.
questoes.explicacao: “Had been removed” is past perfect passive. It places the removal before another past event, “the inspectors arrived”, while the passive construction foregrounds the equipment rather than the agent.

questoes.enunciado: The present perfect in “The company has expanded its operations in recent years” necessarily indicates that the expansion was completed at a specific, finished time in the past.
questoes.explicacao: The present perfect links past developments to the present and is compatible with an unfinished period such as “in recent years”. A specific finished past time normally calls for the simple past.

questoes.enunciado: In “While the researchers were collecting samples, the storm interrupted the work”, the past continuous presents an activity in progress when another past event occurred.
questoes.explicacao: The past continuous “were collecting” sets the ongoing background activity; the simple past “interrupted” marks the event that occurred during it. The conjunction “while” reinforces the overlap.

questoes.enunciado: In “She has been working here since 2021”, the present perfect continuous emphasizes an activity that began in the past and continues up to the present.
questoes.explicacao: The present perfect continuous with “since” marks a starting point in the past and an activity continuing to the present, with emphasis on duration or ongoing activity rather than a completed result.

questoes.enunciado: In reported speech, the verb in “He said that he is tired” must always be changed to “was”, regardless of whether the statement remains true.
questoes.explicacao: Backshift is common after a past reporting verb, but it is not compulsory in every context. A speaker may retain the present tense to present the information as still true or currently relevant.

questoes.enunciado: In “The train leaves at 6:15 tomorrow”, the simple present can express a scheduled future event.
questoes.explicacao: The simple present is regularly used for fixed timetables and schedules, even when the reference is future. The time expression “tomorrow” makes the future reference explicit.

questoes.enunciado: In “I was reading when the lights went out”, the simple past “went out” describes the longer background activity, whereas “was reading” marks the shorter event.
questoes.explicacao: The tense functions are reversed in the statement: “was reading” presents the ongoing background activity, while “went out” marks the shorter event that interrupted it.

questoes.enunciado: In “By next June, they will have completed the bridge”, the future perfect views the completion as occurring before a specified point in the future.
questoes.explicacao: “Will have completed” is the future perfect. It projects the completion before the future reference point “next June”, rather than merely stating that the work will occur at some future time.

questoes.enunciado: In “Applicants must submit the form by Friday”, “must” expresses a strong obligation imposed on applicants.
questoes.explicacao: “Must” commonly expresses strong obligation or requirement. In this context, the deadline and administrative instruction support an obligatory, rather than merely possible, interpretation.

questoes.enunciado: In “You should have checked the figures”, the modal construction expresses an obligation that will have to be fulfilled in the future.
questoes.explicacao: “Should have + past participle” commonly expresses criticism, regret, or an unrealized recommendation concerning the past. It does not impose a future obligation; “should check” would be prospective advice.

questoes.enunciado: In the conditional sentence “If the data were reliable, the conclusion would be stronger”, the speaker presents reliability as an established fact.
questoes.explicacao: This second conditional presents a hypothetical or unreal situation in the present or future. The wording does not establish that the data are reliable; it distances the speaker from that possibility.

questoes.enunciado: In “If the agency had acted earlier, the damage might have been prevented”, the past perfect in the if-clause refers to an unrealized past condition.
questoes.explicacao: The third conditional pattern combines past perfect in the if-clause with a modal perfect in the result clause. It imagines an earlier action that did not occur and a possible alternative past outcome.

questoes.enunciado: The sentence “The documents were signed by the chairperson” is in the passive voice, and “by the chairperson” identifies the agent.
questoes.explicacao: The construction “were signed” uses be + past participle and is passive. The “by”-phrase names the agent who performed the action, although passive sentences can omit the agent.

questoes.enunciado: In “The application can be submitted online”, the modal verb “can” is followed by an active infinitive without “to”.
questoes.explicacao: The modal is followed by the bare infinitive of “be”, but the complete predicate “be submitted” is passive. The structure is modal + be + past participle, not an active infinitive.

questoes.enunciado: In “If you heat ice, it melts”, the present simple in both clauses expresses a general truth rather than a prediction about one particular future event.
questoes.explicacao: This is the zero conditional, commonly used for scientific facts, regular results, and general truths. The present simple in both clauses presents the relationship as generally valid.

questoes.enunciado: In “The proposal may have been rejected”, the modal perfect passive necessarily means that the rejection definitely occurred.
questoes.explicacao: “May have been rejected” expresses uncertainty about a possible past event. The passive form identifies the proposal as the affected entity, while “may” prevents the event from being asserted as certain.

questoes.enunciado: In “The devices, which were tested yesterday, are now available”, the commas indicate that the relative clause adds non-defining information about the devices.
questoes.explicacao: The commas mark a non-defining relative clause, which supplies additional information rather than identifying which devices are meant. Removing it would not fundamentally change the noun phrase’s reference.

questoes.enunciado: In “Each of the candidates submitted their identification”, the word “each” refers to the candidates as a single undivided group and therefore requires a plural verb.
questoes.explicacao: “Each” distributes the reference to individuals and takes a singular verb when it is the subject. In this sentence it is part of the prepositional phrase “of the candidates”; “submitted” agrees with singular “each” understood.

questoes.enunciado: In “Despite the heavy traffic, the ambulance arrived on time”, “despite” introduces a concessive relation and is followed by a noun phrase.
questoes.explicacao: “Despite” is a preposition expressing concession and is followed here by the noun phrase “the heavy traffic”. A finite clause would ordinarily require “although” or “even though”.

questoes.enunciado: In “Each of the candidates were required to show identification”, the verb agrees with the plural noun “candidates”, so the sentence is grammatically correct.
questoes.explicacao: The subject is “each”, not “candidates”, which appears inside the prepositional phrase “of the candidates”. Standard agreement therefore requires the singular form “was required”, not “were required”.

questoes.enunciado: In “Neither the manager nor the assistants was available”, the verb must agree with the nearer subject, “assistants”, and therefore the sentence is grammatically correct.
questoes.explicacao: With “neither...nor”, agreement is commonly guided by the nearer subject in this construction. Because “assistants” is plural, standard proximity agreement calls for “were available”, not “was available”.

questoes.enunciado: In “The committee postponed the meeting because it lacked a quorum”, the pronoun “it” necessarily refers to the meeting.
questoes.explicacao: The most coherent antecedent is “the committee”: the committee lacked a quorum and therefore postponed the meeting. The sentence does not say that the meeting itself lacked a quorum.

questoes.enunciado: In “The results were consistent with those reported earlier”, the demonstrative “those” substitutes for the plural noun “results” and avoids repetition.
questoes.explicacao: “Those” is a demonstrative pronoun referring back to plural “results” and stands for “the results reported earlier”. This substitution creates cohesion and avoids repeating the noun.

questoes.enunciado: In “The measure was introduced in order to reduce costs”, the expression “in order to” introduces a consequence that had already occurred.
questoes.explicacao: “In order to” introduces purpose or intention: reducing costs was the aim of the measure. It does not assert that the reduction was achieved; “as a result” would introduce a consequence.

questoes.enunciado: In “The minister stopped short of endorsing the plan”, the expression “stopped short of” indicates that the minister explicitly approved the plan.
questoes.explicacao: “Stop short of doing something” means not going as far as doing it. The sentence indicates that the minister refrained from endorsing the plan, not that the minister approved it.

questoes.enunciado: In the sentence “Eventually, the researchers found a viable solution”, “eventually” means “possibly” or “by chance”.
questoes.explicacao: “Eventually” means in the end or after some time. It does not mean “possibly” or “by chance”; confusing it with “eventually” in Portuguese as a false friend can distort the chronology.

questoes.enunciado: In “The evidence is far from conclusive”, the phrase “far from” weakens the claim and indicates that the evidence is not conclusive.
questoes.explicacao: “Far from” is an intensifying expression meaning “not at all” or “a long way from”. Thus, the evidence is characterized as clearly insufficient to establish a conclusive result.

questoes.enunciado: In “The figures are actually lower than those published last year”, “actually” is used to emphasize the real situation and is not equivalent to the Portuguese “atualmente”.
questoes.explicacao: “Actually” means in fact or really, whereas “currently” or “nowadays” expresses “atualmente”. Here, it emphasizes the factual comparison and does not locate the figures in the present period.

questoes.enunciado: In “The policy is unlikely to succeed unless funding increases”, the word “unless” can be interpreted as “if ... not” without changing the basic conditional meaning.
questoes.explicacao: “Unless” introduces a negative condition and is equivalent in basic meaning to “if ... not”. The policy’s success is presented as unlikely in the absence of increased funding.

questoes.enunciado: In “The findings were eventually released, despite having been initially withheld”, the participial phrase indicates that the withholding occurred after the release.
questoes.explicacao: “Initially” places the withholding at the beginning of the sequence, while “eventually” places the release later. The participial phrase “having been withheld” refers to an earlier passive event.

questoes.enunciado: In “No sooner had the inspection begun than the alarm sounded”, the inversion after “no sooner” is used to emphasize that the second event followed immediately.
questoes.explicacao: The pattern “no sooner + past perfect + than + simple past” uses subject–auxiliary inversion and conveys that the alarm sounded immediately after the inspection began.

questoes.enunciado: In “The evidence was eventually deemed insufficient”, the word “deemed” means that the evidence was physically damaged or destroyed.
questoes.explicacao: “Deem” means to judge, consider, or regard something as having a particular quality. The sentence says the evidence was judged insufficient; it makes no claim that it was damaged or destroyed.
